The AgroWeb3 : Market Access Window Project will deliver significant socioeconomic benefits at both national and local levels, particularly for smallholder farmers and rural communities in the target regions. These benefits are intertwined with the project's environmental goals, as the economic empowerment of smallholder farmers is directly linked to the promotion of sustainable agricultural practices and the achievement of Global Environmental Benefits (GEBs). Economic Empowerment and Market Access. Smallholder farmers, the primary beneficiaries of the project, will be empowered with the tools and knowledge needed to meet the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) requirements. By providing farmers with satellite-based monitoring and blockchain technology to certify land tenure and demonstrate deforestation-free practices, the project will enhance their ability to access international markets, particularly in the European Union. This access to global markets is critical for improving the livelihoods of smallholder farmers, as it allows them to secure higher incomes by meeting sustainability requirements demanded by buyers. Additionally, the project will help reduce the costs associated with compliance certification. Traditionally, smallholder farmers face significant financial barriers to verifying land tenure and product provenance. By automating these processes through blockchain technology and remote sensing, the project will lower transaction costs and make compliance affordable. This will enhance farmers’ competitiveness in international markets, leading to improved income security and economic resilience. Sustainable Livelihoods and Poverty Reduction. At the local level, the project will promote sustainable land management practices that improve the long-term viability of smallholder farms. By avoiding unsustainable land expansion into forested areas and adopting climate-resilient agricultural practices, farmers will improve the productivity of their land. This will lead to more stable crop yields, enhanced food security, and a reduction in poverty among rural populations. Sustainable agricultural practices will also lead to healthier ecosystems, which support the livelihoods of rural communities by providing critical ecosystem services, such as water regulation and soil fertility. Job Creation and Capacity Building. The project will create new job opportunities through capacity-building initiatives and the establishment of a robust ecosystem for EUDR compliance. Local farmers, agricultural extension officers, and community organizations will receive training in the use of satellite monitoring tools and blockchain technology. This capacity building will equip communities with the skills needed to monitor and verify sustainable practices, manage compliance processes, and support future agricultural innovations. Additionally, the introduction of new technologies will generate jobs related to data management, compliance reporting, and technical support at both the local and national levels. Gender Equality and Social Inclusion. The project will actively promote gender equality by ensuring that women farmers and marginalized groups have equitable access to the tools and resources provided. Women often face additional barriers in accessing land tenure rights and financial resources. By incorporating gender-sensitive approaches in capacity-building programs and ensuring women are prioritized in the training and use of the technology, the project will enhance their role in decision-making processes and increase their economic participation. This will contribute to poverty reduction and create more resilient rural communities by empowering a broader range of stakeholders. Link to Global Environmental and Adaptation Benefits. The socioeconomic benefits delivered by this project directly contribute to Global Environmental Benefits (GEBs) and adaptation outcomes by ensuring that sustainable agricultural practices are both economically viable and environmentally sustainable. By linking market access to the adoption of deforestation-free and climate-resilient practices, the project incentivizes smallholder farmers to actively contribute to environmental goals, such as reducing deforestation, protecting biodiversity, and mitigating climate change. Furthermore, the project’s focus on sustainable livelihoods will enhance the adaptive capacity of rural communities, making them more resilient to climate shocks and environmental degradation. This is especially important in regions prone to climate variability, where food security and economic stability depend on the health of ecosystems and the sustainability of agricultural practices. In summary, the AgroWeb3 : Market Access Window Project will deliver significant socioeconomic benefits that support both local development and global environmental goals. By empowering smallholder farmers, promoting sustainable practices, and fostering inclusive economic growth, the project ensures that the direct beneficiaries contribute meaningfully to broader global efforts to protect ecosystems and mitigate climate change.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To develop a digital tool that supports smallholder farmers in complying with the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) by integrating satellite monitoring and blockchain technology for land tenure verification, product provenance, and sustainable agricultural practices
